evidence.summary: A fixed module-level category list: food, travel, home, other.
Expenses are kept in an in-memory list; nothing is persisted.
add(amount_cents, category, note='') raises ValueError('unknown category') for a category not in the list, else appends {amount_cents, category, note}.

architecture.backend: single Python module exposing an add() function

features.name: Record an expense
features.description: Add an expense with an amount in cents, a category and an optional note.
features.observed_behaviour: add() validates the category, then appends the expense to an in-memory list.
features.business_logic: Amount is integer cents (by name; type not enforced). Category is required and must be in the list. Note defaults to empty.

features.name: Expense categories
features.description: A fixed set of categories (food, travel, home, other); an expense with any other category is rejected.
features.observed_behaviour: CATEGORIES list; add() raises ValueError('unknown category') when the category is not in it.
features.business_logic: Allowed values: food, travel, home, other. Matching is exact and case-sensitive. 'other' is the catch-all. No user-defined categories.

entities.name: Expense
entities.description: A spending record: amount in cents, a category, an optional note

fields.name: amount_cents
fields.description: Amount in cents; currency not recorded

error_handling.behaviour: raises ValueError('unknown category'); nothing is stored

unknowns: No currency, date, merchant, owner or id on an expense; the app has no notion of them.
No persistence: expenses live only in memory, so there is no existing Spendly data to migrate (confirm the user has none stored elsewhere).
No UI, API or entry point; how the user runs it is not in the folder.
